t: 3555. Smallest Subarray to Sort in Every Sliding Window
o: For each window of length k, find the shortest contiguous piece that, when sorted, makes the whole window non-decreasing (0 if already sorted). With n ≤ 1000, recomputing per window is cheap. The classic technique: locate the first and last 'descent' (positions where a[i] > a[i+1]); everything between them contains disorder; then expand outward past elements greater than the segment min (left) or less than the segment max (right).
k: If a window has no adjacent inversion it is already sorted → answer 0.
The disordered core spans from just before the first descent to just after the last descent.
Expand left while the previous element exceeds the core's minimum, and right while the next element is below the core's maximum.

a.n: Approach 1: Sort each window and diff
a.i: Compare the window against its sorted copy; the first and last mismatching indices delimit the minimal segment. O(k log k) per window, trivially correct, and ideal for explaining the goal.
s: For each window start, copy and sort the window.
Skip leading matches; if none mismatch, append 0.
Otherwise find the last mismatch and append its distance from the first.
a.t: O(n·k log k) — sorting each of the n−k+1 windows

a.i: Within a window, find the first index i with nums[i] > nums[i+1] and the last such index j (segment nums[i..j+1] is disordered). Take mn and mx of nums[i..j+1]; extend the left boundary while the element to the left exceeds mn, and the right boundary while the element to the right is below mx. This is O(k) per window with no sorting.
s: Scan for the first descent i; none → answer 0.
Scan backwards for the last descent; the disordered core is [i, j+1].
Compute core min and max; expand left/right greedily.
a.t: O(n·k) — linear scan per window, no sorting

w: For an interview, lead with the sort-and-diff version (obviously correct), then offer the descent/expansion method as the O(nk) refinement — it is the sliding-window generalization of LeetCode 581 'Shortest Unsorted Continuous Subarray'. Pitfalls: forgetting the expansion step (e.g., [1,3,2,4] needs [3,2] only, but [2,1,3,5,4] style windows need growth past the core), and mishandling equal elements (non-decreasing means equal neighbors are fine). Edge cases: k = 1 (always 0), fully reversed window (answer k). Follow-up: solve for all windows in O(n log n) with monotonic stacks and sparse tables if n were 1e5.
